n1de3f9a4fe5.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Bhabha's three-stage nuclear power programme – Uranium-based
First UN Conference on the Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy – Geneva
Geneva Conference on the Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy – 1955
President of the 1955 Geneva conference – Homi Bhabha
n1de3f9a4fe5.x: Bhabha's three-stage programme is thorium-based, not uranium-based; he presided over the first UN Conference on the Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy at Geneva in 1955.

nphysics-9-9.x: J.J. Thomson worked at the Cavendish Laboratory, Cambridge; Chicago and Columbia are linked with Fermi.

n91c1c9f44b2.s: M.S. Swaminathan, known for high-yielding dwarf wheat and rice, chaired the:
o: Scientific Advisory Council to the PM
n91c1c9f44b2.x: Swaminathan chaired the National Commission on Farmers; the Scientific Advisory Council to the PM was headed by C.N.R. Rao.

n819a2b7e2bc.x: Birbal Sahni is associated with palaeobotany; plant embryology is Maheshwari's, cereal rusts K.C. Mehta's and protein structure G.N. Ramachandran's field.

n07827e1670a.s: The Nobel Prize in Economics was added in:
n07827e1670a.x: Economics was added in 1968 and first awarded in 1969; it was not among the original five prizes of Nobel's will.

n8d6bba6b459.s: Who received the Nobel Prize in Physics twice, in 1956 and 1972?
n8d6bba6b459.x: John Bardeen won the Physics Nobel in 1956 and 1972; Bohr won in 1922 and Heisenberg in 1932.

nd92667d2bf2.s: How many disciplines are covered by the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize?
nd92667d2bf2.x: The Bhatnagar Prize covers seven disciplines, from biology to physics; political science is not one of them.

new.s: Who was the first Indian woman to obtain a Western medicine degree (MD, Pennsylvania, 1886)?
new.x: Anandibai Joshi took an MD in Pennsylvania in 1886; Sohonie was the first woman science PhD (1939).

new.s: Janaki Ammal, the plant breeding pioneer at Coimbatore, is known for developing hybrids of:
new.x: Janaki Ammal developed sugarcane hybrids at Coimbatore.

new.s: Who was the first woman to receive a D.Sc. from an Indian university (Calcutta, 1944)?
new.x: Asima Chatterjee took the first women's D.Sc. from Calcutta in 1944; Sohonie's 1939 Cambridge PhD is a different first.

new.s: In 2019, the IAU named the star HD 86081 'Bibha' after which particle physicist?
new.x: The star was named after Bibha Chowdhuri, who did cosmic-ray work with D.M. Bose.

new.s: C.V. Raman founded the Indian Academy of Sciences in:
new.x: Raman founded the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934 and the Raman Research Institute in 1948.

new.s: The Raman Effect refers to:
o: Emission of electrons from a metal by light
Thermal ionisation of atoms in stars
Change in wavelength of scattered light
new.x: The Raman Effect is the change in wavelength of scattered light, discovered on 28 February 1928.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about C.V. Raman?
o: He was the first Indian director of IISc
He founded the Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics
He first studied the harmonic nature of tabla and mridangam
new.x: The Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics was founded by Meghnad Saha; the other statements about Raman are true.

new.x: The AEC was set up in 1948 with Bhabha as first chairman; TIFR dates from 1945.

new.s: The Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (1954), was renamed BARC in:
new.x: AEET was renamed BARC in 1967, after Bhabha died in the 1966 Air India crash.

new.s: Bhabha scattering refers to the scattering between:

new.s: Which honour did Homi Bhabha receive in 1942?
new.x: Bhabha won the Adams Prize in 1942; his Padma Bhushan came in 1954.

new.x: Einstein translated the paper for Zeitschrift fur Physik, giving Bose-Einstein statistics; Dirac named the bosons.

new.s: S.N. Bose received the Padma Vibhushan in:
new.x: S.N. Bose got the Padma Vibhushan in 1954 and became FRS in 1958.

new.s: The year 2012 was observed as National Mathematical Year to mark Ramanujan's:
new.x: 2012 marked the 125th birth anniversary of Ramanujan (born 1887).

new.s: Srinivasa Ramanujan was born on 22 December 1887 at:
new.x: Ramanujan was born at Erode, Tamil Nadu; Chidambaram is Ramakrishnan's birthplace.

o: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science

new.s: Meghnad Saha was elected to the Lok Sabha in:
new.x: Saha, chief architect of river planning, was elected to the Lok Sabha in 1952.

new.s: Niels Bohr, the Father of Atomic Physics, belonged to:
new.x: Bohr was Danish (Copenhagen), not German.

new.s: Who is known as the Father of Nuclear Physics?
new.x: Rutherford is the Father of Nuclear Physics; Fermi is the Architect of the Nuclear Age and Oppenheimer the Father of the atomic bomb.

new.s: J.C. Bose was elected Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in:
new.x: J.C. Bose became FRS in 1920; 1917 was the year he was knighted and founded the Bose Institute.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: S.N. Bose worked on quantum statistics (bosons); Saha is thermal ionisation, Bhabha cosmic rays, J.C. Bose plant physiology.

new.s: C.N.R. Rao was awarded the Bharat Ratna in:
new.x: C.N.R. Rao got the Bharat Ratna in 2014; Kalam in 1997 and Swaminathan in 2024.

new.s: Which solid-state and materials chemist headed the Scientific Advisory Council to the Prime Minister?
new.x: C.N.R. Rao, the foremost solid-state and materials chemist, headed the Scientific Advisory Council to the PM.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about scientists honoured with the Bharat Ratna:

new.x: Kalam was project director of SLV-3, which placed Rohini in orbit in 1980.

new.x: Kalam was chief executive of IGMDP, which developed Agni.

new.s: Who was the first Indian woman to fly in a fighter aircraft (Sukhoi-30, 25 November 2009)?
new.x: President Pratibha Patil flew the Sukhoi-30 in 2009, after Kalam's 2006 flight.

new.s: The Sriharikota launch centre SHAR is named after:
new.x: SHAR is named after ISRO Chairman Satish Dhawan, associated with Aryabhata.

new.s: Who was the first Indian inducted into the Satellite Hall of Fame?
new.x: U.R. Rao, ISRO Chairman 1984-94, was the first Indian in the Satellite Hall of Fame.

new.s: Anil Kakodkar is associated with the development of the:

new.s: Pokhran-II is associated with:
o: Anil Kakodkar and A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
new.x: Pokhran-II was led by Kakodkar and Kalam; Pokhran-I (1974) was Raja Ramanna's.

new.s: K. Kasturirangan, ISRO Chairman 1994-2003, is also associated with drafting the:
new.x: Kasturirangan drafted NEP 2020; the National Commission on Farmers report was Swaminathan's.

new.x: Whittaker proposed five kingdoms; Schleiden and Schwann gave cell theory and Sutton and Boveri the chromosomal theory.

o: Khorana received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1968
Ramakrishnan received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009
Khorana received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009
Ramakrishnan studied the atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit

new.s: Har Gobind Khorana is credited with making the first:
new.x: Khorana made the first synthetic gene and read the genetic code.

new.s: What is the upper age limit for the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize?
new.x: The Bhatnagar Prize, given by CSIR since 1958, has an age limit of 45.

new.s: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar, after whom the CSIR prize is named, was:
o: Founder-director and first DG of CSIR
First recipient of the Vigyan Ratna
new.x: Bhatnagar was the founder-director and first Director-General of CSIR.

new.s: Under the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar, the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize has been absorbed as:

new.x: The Nobel Foundation was set up in 1900, after the 1895 will; the first prizes followed in 1901.

new.x: Economics was added in 1968 and is not in Nobel's will; the original five were Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature and Peace.

new.x: Above about 1.44 solar masses a star cannot remain a white dwarf and becomes a neutron star or black hole.

new.x: Akshay Venkatesh won the Fields Medal in 2018; Manjul Bhargava in 2014.

new.x: The Fields Medal is for mathematicians under 40; 45 is the Bhatnagar limit.

new.x: Banerjee shared the 2019 prize with Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer for fighting global poverty.
